doc.title: Joey Morant interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 2, 2013

chapter: Charleston bands and learning to think
title: Combo Ork book, repertoire of 5,500 songs and caring
summary: He learned to read from the Combo Ork and Latin books, claims 5,500 songs including ethnic ones, and says one must learn to care.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: What we played: tunes and repertoire in the early days

blocks.x: I know what you’re talking about.

Yeah. And then I learned the Latin book too. I know that’s how I built my repertoire. You know, “Charmaine” “Maria Elena” — I know at least fifty-five hundred songs. Go as far back as you want. Ethnic songs too. Greek songs, Irish, Italian, Russian songs. I’m the only band that goes to Moscow that plays “Moscow Nights” at the end of the concert [scats]. And they start dancing when I play that. But the other bands don’t know it. Either they didn’t care to learn it, never heard it before, or it doesn’t matter to them. So through all of the questions you ask me, you have to learn to care. I care about you. I look at your office and I see character. I see persona. I see a world. I see story. I see heartache. I see hurt, I see love. I see things maybe even your wife don’t see. I’ll challenge her. I see things. She ain’t me you know. And that’s why I try to show you without being overbearing. Like you made me happy just stepping in the room. Well you can’t be happy © Fillius Jazz Archive -8-

unless you feel what I feel. A lot of people come in here and look at your books. What I see is intrinsic in the air, in the mortar in the room, it’s in the bricks. The room is an animal. It has a head, a body, arms, tail, legs, feet.
